findings.finding: Reported raw mean and optimized utility are different objectives
findings.evidence: In the first instrumented2s tree, bid1 raw mean7.0050 exceeds bid4 6.9845, but average tanh utilities .306466 vs .307439 reverse order; UCT and visits follow transformed utility.
findings.limit: The tanh transform is deliberate risk shaping, not proof of an arithmetic/backprop bug. Changing it also changes UCB relative scaling.

findings.finding: Continuation estimates depend heavily on tree expansion
findings.evidence: Paired4096-scene policy-only rollout means bid1=8.9615 vs bid4=7.9730, paired difference .98845 with standard error .13055. Full tree2s picks4; root-only and two-decision-layer probes pick1.
findings.limit: Different tree depths induce different continuation policies. No full-game optimality oracle for this real4p position; this does not establish which tree statistic causes the bias.

findings.finding: The symptom persists across UCT, SH and DPW in this fixture
findings.evidence: All three2s probes choose4 under original utility; isolated linear utility2s chooses1.
findings.limit: Single case and one timing per setting are diagnostic, not held-out strength validation.

followup.finding: Frozen original tree evaluated on held-out paired scenarios favors bid1 under original tanh objective, whereas exploration returns recommend bid4 at 32768 iterations. Original at 131072 recommends bid1. Linear returns alone also flip with budget. Supports finite-budget exploratory-continuation bias; no validated general production repair.
